title: Three Leaders, One First: Trump, Xi and Putin Meet
summary:
It was the photo seen around the world. For the first time ever, the leaders of the United States, China and Russia sat down together for a formal meeting. President Donald Trump walked with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and the three countries released a joint statement.

The statement promised to release more oil and, for the first time, to hold formal talks about nuclear weapons. The United States, Russia and China are the world's three preeminent nuclear powers. The meeting lasted just over 80 minutes.

President Trump said the meeting went great and built fantastic relationships. President Putin called it the beginning of a new era of global diplomacy. But the countries still have deep divisions, and the joint statement is light on specifics. American officials were especially keen to highlight the part about arms control, after years of China resisting American requests for talks on nuclear weapons.

The declaration also included a promise to pump more oil and criticism of the International Criminal Court. The United States is trying to weaken the court, while the court is trying to arrest Putin over war crimes in Ukraine. The leaders also agreed to plan a future dialogue to reduce nuclear risks.

Much of the attention was on body language. At one point, Xi held Trump's arm. Earlier, Trump joked and embraced Putin at a separate meeting, and the Kremlin said Putin left in an "excellent mood."

Not everyone was cheering. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said, "Mr. Putin is not our friend, nor will he ever be." Trump argues that only his personal connections with strong leaders can produce progress. The world will be watching to see what the promises turn into.
why_it_matters: When the world's three biggest nuclear powers talk, it can lower the risk of conflict — but the statement is light on specifics, so the real test is what happens next.

background_read: The United States, China and Russia are three of the world's most powerful countries, and each has nuclear weapons.
Leaders of powerful countries usually meet one at a time, so a meeting of all three at once is unusual.
Nuclear weapons are extremely powerful weapons, and countries talk about arms control to limit the risk of them being used.
The International Criminal Court is a court that tries people accused of very serious crimes such as war crimes.
